sessions.label: turn-3
replies:
The guide (the page repeats the same text four times) lists these tools:

- 5 mm hex key for the mounting bolt
- Cable cutter that cuts cleanly without fraying
- Chain tool or quick-link pliers
- Phillips screwdriver for the limit screws
- A little grease for the bolt threads

A bike stand helps, or you can turn the bike upside down on a soft mat. The guide also says to check that the derailleur hanger is straight, since a bent one causes most poor shifting. The new derailleur's torque is usually 8–10 Nm, so you'd need a torque wrench to hit it. The guide doesn't list one, but the figure is printed on the derailleur body.

Order a quick link that matches your chain's speed count, in case the old one can't be reused. I'm assuming that detail applies to your bike.

replies:
Try a chickpea and spinach stew with tomato, garlic and smoked paprika, served over rice or with crusty bread. It takes about 25 minutes and has no cashews.

- Fry sliced garlic in olive oil, then add the paprika and a pinch of cumin.
- Add a tin of chopped tomatoes and a tin of drained chickpeas, and simmer for 10 minutes.
- Stir in a few handfuls of spinach until it wilts, then add lemon juice and salt.

Use sweet smoked paprika rather than hot, since you don't like very spicy food. There's no raw onion, so no heartburn trouble either.
